To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 8-AG resistance of the mouse cell line A9 is due to a missense mutation in the HGPRT structural gene, while the 8- AG resistance of the mouse line RAG may be due to a recessive regulatory gene.

(a) the HGPRT activity in the 8-aza resistant A9 cells is different from that of wild type, (b) the HGPTR activity in A9 is very heat labile, (c) the HGPRI in A9 binds the substrate guanine much more tightly than that of normal cells, and (d) A9 has no cross-reacting material to normal HGPRT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of genetic alterations in mammalian cells.
the nature of molecular alterations conferring the mutant phenotype in two stable mouse cell lines, A9 and RGA, resistant to 8-AZAGUANINE.
the molecular basis of 8-azaguaine resistance in mouse cell lines, and with the possible relationship between the nature of the mutation and the mechanism of reversion to the normal phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the A9 and RGA mutants are both deficient in HGPRT, but the molecular nature of the defect is different in the two cell lines.
the A9 mutation involves the structural gene for HGPRT.
A9 is a mutant with a structurally altered enzyme, while RAG is a mutant with altered regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 8-AG resistant mutants are defective in the HGPRT gene, and are probably due to point mutations within the structural gene.
the HGPRT activity of A9 is a modified form of normal HGPRT which is not immunologically related to the normal enzyme.
the A9 mutation is probably a structural alteration in the HGPRT gene, while the RAG mutation could be due to the loss of an essential regulatory gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to study the nature of mutations conferring drug resistance in mouse cells.
a single amino acid change within the HGPRT molecule can confer 8-azaguaine resistance to a mouse cell.
the HGPRT activity in A9 is different from the normal enzyme in both its heat stability and kinetic properties, suggesting that the mutation may be in the structural gene.
